title: 428. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Solving Elementary Tangent Equations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Two solutions of a tangent equation in one turn
questions.learningObjective: Solve a basic tangent equation on one full turn in degrees.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\tan x=1\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle is \(45^\circ\). Tangent is positive in Quadrants I and III, so the solutions are \(45^\circ\) and \(180^\circ+45^\circ=225^\circ\). At \(135^\circ\), in Quadrant II, the tangent is \(-1\).
questions.hint: Tangent repeats every \(180^\circ\); add \(180^\circ\) to the first solution.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a tangent equation with right side zero on one full turn.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\tan x=0\) with \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\), the tangent is \(0\) exactly when \(\sin x=0\), which happens at \(x=0\) and \(x=\pi\) in this interval. At \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) the cosine is \(0\), so the tangent is undefined there.
questions.hint: A fraction is zero when its numerator is zero and its denominator is not.

questions.concept: Tangent equation with a negative value
questions.learningObjective: Solve a tangent equation with a negative right side on one full turn in radians.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\tan x=-\sqrt{3}\) with \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle is \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), since \(\tan\frac{\pi}{3}=\sqrt{3}\). Tangent is negative in Quadrants II and IV, so \(x=\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{2\pi}{3}\) or \(x=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{5\pi}{3}\). The angles \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) and \(\frac{4\pi}{3}\) have tangent \(+\sqrt{3}\).
questions.hint: Use the quadrants where sine and cosine have opposite signs.

questions.concept: General solution of a tangent equation
questions.learningObjective: Write the general solution of a basic tangent equation using its period.
questions.question: What is the general solution of \(\tan x=1\), where \(k\) is any integer?
questions.explanation: The tangent has period \(\pi\), so every solution is obtained from \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) by adding a multiple of \(\pi\). The formula with \(2k\pi\) gives only half of the solutions; for example, it misses \(\frac{5\pi}{4}\), where the tangent is also \(1\).
questions.hint: Recall the period of the tangent function.

questions.learningObjective: Isolate the tangent before solving a linear trigonometric equation.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(\sqrt{3}\tan x-1=0\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Isolate the tangent: \(\tan x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\). The reference angle is \(30^\circ\), and tangent is positive in Quadrants I and III: \(x=30^\circ\) or \(x=210^\circ\). The angles \(60^\circ\) and \(240^\circ\) have tangent \(\sqrt{3}\), the reciprocal value.
questions.hint: Solve for \(\tan x\) and decide which standard angle has that tangent.

questions.concept: Counting solutions of a tangent equation
questions.learningObjective: Count the solutions of a tangent equation on one full turn.
questions.question: How many solutions does \(\tan x=5\) have with \(0\le x<2\pi\)?
questions.explanation: The tangent has period \(\pi\) and takes every real value exactly once in each period. The interval \([0,2\pi)\) has length \(2\pi\), which is two periods, so there are two solutions: \(x=\tan^{-1}(5)\) and \(x=\tan^{-1}(5)+\pi\).
questions.hint: Compare the length of the interval with the period of tangent.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a tangent equation on the open interval between two consecutive asymptotes.
questions.question: What is the solution of \(\tan x=-1\) with \(-\frac{\pi}{2}<x<\frac{\pi}{2}\)?
questions.explanation: Tangent is odd, so \(\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-\tan\frac{\pi}{4}=-1\), and \(-\frac{\pi}{4}\) lies in the interval. The angle \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) also has tangent \(-1\), but it is greater than \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) and so lies outside the interval.
questions.hint: A negative tangent in this interval corresponds to a negative angle.

questions.learningObjective: Use the range of tangent to decide whether an equation has solutions.
questions.question: Does the equation \(\tan x=1000\) have a real solution?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because the tangent takes every real value.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the tangent must lie between \(-1\) and \(1\).

questions.explanation: The tangent is a ratio \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\), and as \(x\) approaches \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) from below the cosine approaches \(0\) while the sine approaches \(1\), so the tangent grows without bound. Its range is all real numbers, so \(\tan x=1000\) has solutions. The restriction to \([-1,1]\) applies to sine and cosine only.
questions.hint: Consider what happens to \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) as \(x\) approaches \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).

questions.concept: Tangent equation with a decimal value
questions.learningObjective: Use a given inverse tangent value to list all solutions on one full turn.
questions.question: Given that \(\tan^{-1}(2.5)\approx 68.2^\circ\), what are all solutions of \(\tan x=2.5\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\), to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: The first solution is \(68.2^\circ\). Tangent has period \(180^\circ\), so the second solution is \(68.2^\circ+180^\circ=248.2^\circ\). The angle \(111.8^\circ=180^\circ-68.2^\circ\) is in Quadrant II, where the tangent is negative.
questions.hint: Tangent is positive in Quadrants I and III; add the period of tangent to the first solution.

questions.learningObjective: Rearrange a linear equation in tangent before solving it on one full turn.
questions.question: What are all solutions of \(3\tan x+5=\tan x+3\) with \(0^\circ\le x<360^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Collect terms: \(2\tan x=-2\), so \(\tan x=-1\). The reference angle is \(45^\circ\), and tangent is negative in Quadrants II and IV: \(x=180^\circ-45^\circ=135^\circ\) or \(x=360^\circ-45^\circ=315^\circ\). The angles \(45^\circ\) and \(225^\circ\) solve \(\tan x=+1\).
questions.hint: Solve the linear equation for \(\tan x\) and keep track of the sign before choosing quadrants.
